newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: U.S. drug agency to open in Nicaragua in 1997.
newsitem.headline: U.S. drug agency to open in Nicaragua in 1997.

text.p: The United States will open an anti-drug office in Managua in 1997, U.S. Ambassador to Nicaragua John Maisto said on Thursday.
"I have the guarantee ... that the DEA (Drug Enforcement Administration) will open an office here in 1997, with security," Maisto said at a news conference.

Maisto, who leaves Nicaragua on Friday, said he wanted a DEA office opened in Managua in 1996, but budget limitations precluded it. The DEA office in neighbouring Costa Rica currently handles Nicaraguan drug-trafficking cases.
Nicaragua in recent years has increasingly become a drug trans-shipment point between Colombia and the United States.
"There is a growing drug trafficking problem here, especially on the Atlantic coast, but not exclusively on the Atlantic coast," Maisto said.

In April 1996, in its largest drug bust to date, Nicaraguan police with DEA help seized 3,080 pounds (1,400 kgs) of cocaine on a fishing boat called the Neptune III off its Atlantic Coast near the city of Bluefields, 240 miles (380 kms) east of Managua.
Officials in Nicaragua say they lack the money and personnel needed to patrol the country's long, sparsely populated Atlantic coast.
The U.S. government did not open a DEA office in Nicaragua in the 1980s due to its hostile relations with the left-wing Sandinista government at the time, which ruled with Soviet and Cuban backing.
Following the Sandinista's fall in the 1990 elections, and the growing separation of the Nicaraguan police from the Sandinista party, relations between the DEA and local police improved.
